# local-modeling

Build bounded implementation models and attributed checkers from a selected audit question.

Use [guide.md](guide.md). Only controller-loaded references are available; links do not grant file access. Return the requested typed proposal; request missing source.

VERIFICATION METHOD SELECTION TLA+ is a verification/search method, not the definition of success. When a direct executable trace can confirm or refute the selected obligation, describe that test first: legal prehistory, controlled events, observations and oracle. Prefer a local model when interleavings or state-space exploration are the hard part. Record the preferred_check in the typed question: direct_test/controlled_schedule use the implementation-check route; local_model uses this method and the existing TLC, experiment and evidence checks. Model behavior from code and properties from obligations. No result under finite test/model bounds establishes whole-system correctness; an agent judgment cannot replace actual execution, supported observation or calibration.

MODELING METHOD Before generating actions, trace the selected obligation through concrete control flow. For each relevant state read/write, identify its source binding, owner, and persistence or recovery contract. Split actions at actual interruptible boundaries: blocking calls, channel operations, callbacks, lock release, and storage completion. Compare checks at start with checks at completion; ask whether identity, context, configuration, or inputs can change in between. Do not combine separated effects into an atomic action without evidence. For each action enumerate changed variables, unchanged variables, permitted failures, and observable effects. Retain error branches and reachable boundary values. Derive scheduling and fault assumptions from the selected scope, not from the property being tested. Separately define the property trigger and consequence. Map each checker to its claim and scope. Every configured invariant must exist and must not be smuggled into Init/Next as an assumption. State which selected obligations this model checks and which remain pending. Properties can fail. Bound participants, contexts, outstanding operations and failures explicitly. Bounds must preserve the candidate violation and be recorded in scope/constants. Calibration establishes only that finite actual observations have an explaining model path. For ordinary technical repair, preserve the entire Properties module and observable property descriptions byte-for-byte. If property syntax itself is invalid and semantic preservation cannot be established, report a gap for explicit semantic investigation; do not replace the predicate with TRUE or weaken its trigger.

EXECUTION COVERAGE AND OBSERVABILITY Connect model assumptions and scope to the selected audit question. For selected behaviors, facts, declare bounded reachability requirements: named zero-argument state predicates in Behavior, linked claim_ids and behavior_ids/fact_ids. The controller checks whether these triggers can occur using auxiliary TLC searches. State why a trigger is inapplicable rather than inventing one. An invariant holds result alone cannot demonstrate an interaction whose trigger was never reached. Never add guards or state constraints that hide the behavior under investigation. Broader obligation observation requires consequence_observations with material-backed bindings, actual required participants and events. Partial or single-participant observations cannot establish an unobserved cluster broader violation. Inconclusive calibration remains inconclusive; exploratory search is allowed but does not confirm implementation behavior. Model search reuse requires matching semantic inputs and an explicit source execution record; identical invariant names or scope prose are insufficient.

STAGED DELIVERY The current modeling brief is the working input; archived reviews are not a substitute for actual necessary source. Use relevant unresolved counterevidence and resolved conclusions with source references, not an assumed clean slate. Save justified model components before experiment assembly is complete. ModelDraft requires explicit pending_work, including harness and observation. A draft with core behavior/property gaps is not executable. Keep properties separate from code behavior even for a partial draft. A complete Bundle is still accepted in one call. Check the actual generated constant assignments and invariant declarations against the selected question; intentions or a model filename do not establish coverage. SANY parsing, finite exploratory search, real trace calibration, and implementation confirmation are distinct outcomes. Completing only a harness cannot change the saved model's semantics. A changed behavior interpretation needs normal F1/F3 or semantic F2 handling and applicable rechecking, not reuse of a same-name checker.

Generate a complete Bundle, or save a ModelDraft with explicit pending components, for the selected obligation and code workset: implementation behavior, separate property checkers, an explicit observation projection, and an executable harness calling actual target code. Do not return a reference model presented as an implementation abstraction. Use MODULE Behavior with Init, Next, vars, and Obs operators. Obs must be a record with scalar integer, boolean, or string fields; a bounded sequence of such records is supported for explicitly complete observed histories. Use MODULE Properties EXTENDS Behavior for invariant operators; no checked invariant may occur as a guard or assumption in Behavior. Only standard modules Naturals, Integers, Sequences, FiniteSets, Bags and Reals are supported. Do not use INSTANCE, LOCAL, ASSUME, TLC, Java overrides, module-qualified operators (EXCEPT ![key] updates are allowed), IO, JSON modules, state constraints, action constraints, symmetry, or operator replacement. Inline constant definitions or return constant assignments. The framework writes INIT/NEXT/invariant configuration. Open dictionaries in the wire schema use key/value_json entries; preserve nonempty parameter values; record bounds in constants and the scope description. Do not invent atomicity or omit existing error branches. Model successful and failed effects based on source; distinguish unconfirmed external contracts. The harness must call the existing implementation. Do not change its protocol code. Follow the execution-backend harness instructions in the structured input. Never call shell/subprocess/network services or read outside the working directory. Emit lines prefixed CA_EVENT followed by JSON objects with event (string) and state (object) using actual observed values; emit an initial observation before the first transition. Include facts such as operation_started, context_changed, operation_completed only when they really occurred. Do not print a precomputed expected trace. Emit all state fields required by the observation projection at every observation. Use deterministic short experiments, report adaptation differences and missing controls. Do not pretend in-memory reconstruction is a power-loss durability test. Use the supplied trace-output protocol and real runtime values. Keep the state space small but preserve interruptible writes, historical constraints, errors, and required participants. Explain what is excluded and whether the target consequence is observable. Properties may fail; do not repair behavior by importing the required property. If a scoped implementation model cannot be justified, record the uncertainty explicitly.

Bundle.checkers must explicitly map each invariant to its claim and Scope; never rely on independent list ordering. Event monitors are optional; supported shared descriptions are event_assertion and stable_support over actual observed fields. An EventMonitor must reference its shared checker definition and identify selected code bindings, attributed grounding and observable applicability conditions. Partial observations cannot establish a violation by selecting a bad hidden model state. A weaker documented acceptance contract is different from violating an established durability guarantee; preserve uncertain cases.

For supported automatic checker/monitor correspondence, supply observable_properties and set properties to the exact marker GENERATE_FROM_OBSERVABLE_PROPERTIES. The framework generates the Properties module. Each EventMonitor references checker_id; trigger, assertion and identity_fields live only in that shared property. Scalar raw fields must have a unique observation projection. All configured checkers must have shared descriptions when using this path. For arbitrary TLA properties, do not use the marker; monitor correspondence remains unestablished. An event_assertion describes trigger => assertion over observed fields, for example trigger field state.completed eq true and assertion field state.ready eq true, with explicit model projections for both. This is a wire-format example, not a candidate obligation for the current implementation. A stable_support description compares the assertion.field object across effective events (trigger) sharing identity_fields, with history_field pointing to a complete observed sequence. History entry keys must be simple identifiers. The history must actually match recorded events; never emit a fabricated history to satisfy calibration.

Before requesting dependencies, consult file_lookup for exact line counts and file_metadata for previously read intervals. A range already in storage but omitted here may be requested for this task. Use reading_purpose=context only when acquired or reattached material can be returned to this same task without changing graph meaning or selected code scope. Use dependency when actual new bindings or paths must be connected to the existing unit. An accepted dependency scope can precede any model; do not create a placeholder model for F3 eligibility. Include actual supporting behavior without treating its unverified guarantees as assumptions or automatically checking every associated obligation.

ConstraintSource.source_ids contains only acquired material IDs. For source_kind=code_observation, provide separate nonempty binding_ids selected by this unit, and source_ids covering their actual material ranges. # Context and history in a local consensus question

Input: the selected question, attributed obligations, actual source mappings and unresolved boundaries. Output: a compact context analysis in the Bundle, with links to concrete variables, actions, checkers and reachability requirements. This is an implementation abstraction, not a new normative specification.

Identify applicable dimensions independently: participant identity, operation/object identity, epoch/view, execution phase, position and configuration version. Unknown or inapplicable dimensions need a source-grounded explanation. Do not compress all dimensions into one global round.

Trace support through production, send, receive, acceptance, retention and consumption. Explain which guarantee each event establishes, the code implementing it and which upstream contracts remain unchecked. Different participants may occupy different contexts concurrently.

At a context change, retain outstanding requests, callbacks, messages and evidence unless actual code cancels, partitions or legally consumes them. An old operation may complete safely on its original object. Object or channel isolation can substitute for an explicit numeric-context comparison; missing a familiar guard alone is not a defect. Previously established facts may remain valid across context changes when the implementation permits it.

Separate in-context aggregation from replacement of the aggregation object or configuration. A monotonic update inside one object lifetime does not imply monotonic state across destruction and reconstruction. A phase name is not a lock or atomicity boundary. Split actions at observed queues, blocking calls, callbacks, lock release and persistence completion.

Distinguish volatile reconstruction from crash recovery; persistence survival follows the actual store contract. Same-context restart may be legal. Never inject Byzantine behavior into a crash-only scope or add an absent guard to satisfy a property.

For each modeled crossing, name the retained operation identity, source bindings, start/change/completion actions and the checker. Supply an executable same-history reachability requirement if claiming ordered interaction coverage. Separate reachable points cannot establish their ordered joint execution. State which dimensions, participants or paths are excluded. An arithmetic-only instance can mark cross-context networking not applicable while retaining report truth and configuration history as unchecked boundaries.

Check the emitted Behavior and actual TLC configuration: declared transitions must be enabled, checkers configured, trigger witnesses correlated to the same object/history. Agent explanation is a correspondence proposal; actual reachability and checker runs supply separate evidence. Never treat a single-node observation as evidence about unobserved participants.

EXPERIMENT AND OBSERVATION METHOD Locate observation points at actual implementation effects, distinguishing operation start, internal completion, and externally effective return. Emit actual fields at those points. Associate prerequisites by participant, operation and context, not just event names. State what legal inputs and dependency contracts make the schedule admissible. A replay plan may add observation mapping and monitors without changing model behavior or properties. Missing fields remain missing. A compatible partial trace is not a violation. For model replay, the same finite property description must generate the model checker and monitor before automatic confirmation is possible; an arbitrary matching ID is insufficient. A direct check has no model checker or calibration: its monitor evaluates the saved shared property, and the entire check is reviewed against the selected obligation, actual calls, observations and sources. Unreviewed or disputed correspondence cannot confirm a defect. Use the bounded observable property forms advertised in the schema. Unsupported direct properties require an explicit gap or local_model fallback. Unsupported model properties may still be searched, but require further correspondence investigation before implementation-level confirmation. For stable support, compare ordered effective events for the same identity/context; changing context is not automatically a violation. Complete accumulated history must correspond to the observed events. Report instrumentation differences. Only independently checked observation-only edits may continue to confirmation; protocol mutations or unreviewed changes do not represent the original implementation. Do not claim a review happened merely by returning a flag. After replay: unreached prerequisites permit F4; incompatible behavior requires F1; disputed applicability requires F2; missing boundary producers require F3. Missing tools, compilation errors and budgets are technical limitations, not semantic classifications.

# Local behavior and semantic facts

For a selected behavior record actor, trigger, context, purpose, consumed facts and their actual producers; checks, writes, persistence, sends and callbacks; success/reject/stale/error/partial/configuration branches; external inference; existing protections; interfering events; and the smallest discriminating check.

Separate independent actors and branches whose outputs mean different things. A fact is an established assertion scoped by identity and context, not a raw variable or a mixture of possible outcomes. Observation, notification, durable completion and role transition completion are different facts. Preserve unknown establishment instead of connecting adjacent known activities directly. Do not turn code guards into normative obligations without a justified contract or explicit derivation.

Follow only actual fact dependencies across shared state, request identity, context versions, object replacement, persistence, configuration activation, recovery, reclamation and independent loops. Different event orders alone do not imply a violation. Seek alternate guards, ownership, serialization, generation IDs, persistence-before-reply, later validation and reconstruction; narrow or close suspicions explained by those mechanisms.

Use produces_fact_ids/consumes_fact_ids once. The controller derives reverse indices; there is no independent transfer-edge object. Record unknown producers/consumers in Fact.unknowns. Do not infer a guarantee from queue receipt, a progress update or an unverified caller.

Use actual source identities. Contiguous acquired subranges of one captured version can be registered without new acquisition. Text-view aliases are lookup keys, not citations. Missing source requires reading, not deletion of an evidence dependency. Retain protections and contrary evidence in the current question. Detailed history stays archived; the next workset contains only the selected fact lifecycle, obligation, source, discriminator and check plan.

When Behaviors process related inputs/responses, update the same evidence/context or serve the same consumer, compare context validity, identity correlation, invalidation, errors/partial results, durability and generation/version transitions. An independent asynchronous path updating shared evidence while the main progress path is blocked can justify focused reading. Asymmetry alone is not a defect: establish the weakest source-grounded Fact, locate its actual consumer, determine whether that consumer interprets it more strongly, then seek alternate protections. Preserve both applicable variants and unresolved responsibility.
